Note::diff_lines¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

TokenBatch Note::diff_lines(const Note& other) const

Line-Level Difference Between Two Notes¶

diff_lines(other) compares each cell of self against the matching cell of other one line at a time and returns only the changed lines as a TokenBatch of tag-prefixed tokens. It is the line-granularity member of the diff / align family, alongside nlp().diff_words(), diff_chars, and the equal-included nlp().align_sentences() / nlp().align_tokens().

How the comparison works¶

Each cell pair is split on \n — as split_lines does, without keeping the line terminator, so tokens carry no trailing newline. The two line lists are aligned by their longest common subsequence, and because this is a diff_* method only the lines that differ are emitted, in order, one per token, tagged in the first byte:

Tag

Meaning

In self

In other

-

removed — line in self, not matched in other

yes

no

+

added — line in other, not matched in self

no

yes

Lines identical on both sides produce no token, so a cell with no line-level change contributes an empty range. A line that is edited rather than moved shows as a -/+ pair: the old text leaves, the new text arrives. For a transcript that also keeps the unchanged lines, there is no align_lines spelling — run diff_lines and merge the -/+ tokens back against the original line list.

The TokenBatch result¶

Tokens from all cells are concatenated into the rank-1 Note batch.tokens(). The rank-1 Int64 Note batch.offsets() has length numel + 1 and marks each cell’s run: cell r owns tokens.at(k) for k in [offsets[r], offsets[r + 1]). Unchanged cells have an empty range.

Shape, pairing, and rejections¶

Comparison is per cell and pairwise. self and other must share numel, or one may be a scalar (numel() == 1) broadcast against the other. Rejections raise pluss::Error:

  • bytes-mode self → Note::diff_lines requires a UTF-8 text Note (lhs is bytes).

  • unequal numel, neither side scalar → Note::diff_lines expects equal numel or scalar broadcast.

The alignment is O(m · n) in lines per cell and deterministic: on a tie the - is emitted before the +.

Example 1: An Edited Line And An Appended Line¶

const auto batch = pluss::make_note({"alpha\nbeta\ngamma"})
                       .diff_lines(pluss::make_note({"alpha\nBETA\ngamma\ndelta"}));

std::cout << pluss::note::print(batch.tokens()) << "\n";
std::cout << "offsets: [";
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < batch.offsets().integers().size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << batch.offsets().integers()[i];
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["-beta", "+BETA", "+delta"]
offsets: [0, 3]

alpha and gamma are unchanged. beta is re-cased — -beta out, +BETA in — and delta is appended.

Example 2: Identical Cells Produce Nothing¶

const auto batch = pluss::make_note({"one\ntwo"})
                       .diff_lines(pluss::make_note({"one\ntwo"}));
std::cout << pluss::note::print(batch.tokens()) << "\n";
std::cout << "offsets: [";
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < batch.offsets().integers().size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << batch.offsets().integers()[i];
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[0], dim=1, numel=0, encoding=utf8)
[]
offsets: [0, 0]

Example 3: A Single Inserted Line¶

const auto batch = pluss::make_note({"one\ntwo"})
                       .diff_lines(pluss::make_note({"one\nEXTRA\ntwo"}));
std::cout << pluss::note::print(batch.tokens()) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["+EXTRA"]

one and two stay; only the inserted line is reported.
